exercises.heading: Section 4.6 Exercises
exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find the directional derivative using the limit definition only.

problem.paragraph: $$f\left( {x,y} \right) = 5 - 2x^{2} - \frac{1}{2}y^{2}$$ at point $$P\left( {3,4} \right)$$ in the direction of $$\text{u} = \left( {\cos \frac{\pi}{4}} \right)\mathbf{i} + \left( {\sin \frac{\pi}{4}} \right)\mathbf{j}$$

$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = y^{2}\cos \left( {2x} \right)$$ at point $$P\left( {\frac{\pi}{3},2} \right)$$ in the direction of $$\text{u} = \left( {\cos \frac{\pi}{4}} \right)\mathbf{i} + \left( {\sin \frac{\pi}{4}} \right)\mathbf{j}$$

Find the directional derivative of $$f\left( {x,y} \right) = y^{2}\sin \left( {2x} \right)$$ at point $$P\left( {\frac{\pi}{4},2} \right)$$ in the direction of $$\mathbf{u} = 5\mathbf{i} + 12\mathbf{j}.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, solve the problem.

problem.paragraph: The temperature $$T$$ in a metal sphere is inversely proportional to the distance from the center of the sphere (the origin: $$\left( {0,0,0} \right)).$$ The temperature at point $$\left( {1,2,2} \right)$$ is $$120^\circ \text{C} .$$

list.item: Find the rate of change of the temperature at point $$\left( {1,2,2} \right)$$ in the direction toward point $$\left( {2,1,3} \right).$$
Show that, at any point in the sphere, the direction of greatest increase in temperature is given by a vector that points toward the origin.

problem.paragraph: The electrical potential (voltage) in a certain region of space is given by the function $$V(x,y,z) = 5x^{2} - 3xy + xyz.$$

list.item: Find the rate of change of the voltage at point $$\left( {3,4,5} \right)$$ in the direction of the vector $$\left\langle {1,1,-1} \right\rangle.$$
In which direction does the voltage change most rapidly at point $$\left( {3,4,5} \right)?$$
What is the maximum rate of change of the voltage at point $$\left( {3,4,5} \right)?$$

problem.paragraph: If the electric potential at a point $$\left( {x,y} \right)$$ in the xy-plane is $$V(x,y) = e^{-2x}\cos (2y),$$ then the electric intensity vector at $$\left( {x,y} \right)$$ is $$\mathbf{E} = -\nabla V(x,y).$$

list.item: Find the electric intensity vector at $$\left( {\frac{\pi}{4},0} \right).$$
Show that, at each point in the plane, the electric potential decreases most rapidly in the direction of the vector $$\mathbf{E}.$$

problem.paragraph: In two dimensions, the motion of an ideal fluid is governed by a velocity potential $$\varphi.$$ The velocity components of the fluid $$u$$ in the x-direction and $$v$$ in the y-direction, are given by $$\left\langle {u,v} \right\rangle = \nabla\varphi.$$ Find the velocity components associated with the velocity potential $$\varphi(x,y) = \sin \pi x \sin 2\pi y.$$

solution.paragraph: $$〈 u , v 〉 = 〈 \pi cos ( \pi x ) sin ( 2 \pi y ) , 2 \pi sin ( \pi x ) cos ( 2 \pi y ) 〉 〈 u , v 〉 = 〈 \pi cos ( \pi x ) sin ( 2 \pi y ) , 2 \pi sin ( \pi x ) cos ( 2 \pi y ) 〉$$
